description_full: Metlen Energy & Metals PLC operates as an industrial and energy company focusing on the metals and energy sectors worldwide. The company engages in the development, construction, and operation of thermal power plants; and design and construction of electricity infrastructure projects. It also develops RES and energy storage projects; manages power generation and energy plants; and retails electricity and natural gas supply. In addition, the company engages in the procurement and management of natural gas and other energy products for large B2B corporate clients; and develops large-scale energy projects for electricity production and energy transition. Further, it extracts, processes, and refines alumina, aluminium, bauxite, and various metals and minerals. Additionally, the company undertakes various infrastructure construction projects, such as roadworks, buildings, and railway and port projects, as well as solid and liquid waste management projects; and designs, constructs, operates, finances, and maintains infrastructure, building, environmental, hydraulic, and technology and energy projects. Metlen Energy & Metals PLC was founded in 1908 and is headquartered in Athens, Greece.

financial_summary: METLEN ENERGY & METALS PLC is a mid-cap utilities business with a $8.1B market cap on $7.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 17% against a 7% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 17% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $269M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.0× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 22% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
